messages:
ashwin: Heads up — seeing a 12-18% step slowdown in TP jobs after last night's kernel-selector tweak. Started at ~09:12 UTC on the prod perf harness.

maria: when did the selector change land? which flag?

ashwin: landed in runtime v2.14.3 — we changed heuristics to prefer the 'fast-small-msg' kernel for cudnn-attn on <48KB comms.

dylan: which topology? ring or tree? TP=8, PP=1?

ashwin: 8-way TP (no pipeline), ring default. micro-batch=1, seq=1024, kv-cache warm. Profiling shows all-reduce waits spike and GPUs idle while waiting for late ACK handling.

perf-bot: quick summary (from perf capture):
  - majority wait: ncclSend/ncclRecv enqueue -> host-side cudaEventQuery stalls
  - avg message payload: ~6KB (fragmented into 4KB-ish frames)
  - ring tail latency increased by ~45us per step vs baseline
  - tree fallback has fewer small-packet enqueues but higher per-op overhead for large msgs

maria: interesting — small messages => more packets => more acks. Could the new kernel be emitting different comm packing sizes?

ashwin: yes. Kernel selection changed the tensor chunking boundaries. Previously we packed contiguous KV updates into a single 48KB envelope; new kernel splits into smaller prime-aligned fragments for better compute packing. That reduced kernel latency for single-GPU runs but increased comm ops count.

sam: so it's a tradeoff: compute win vs comm overhead. We didn't test with TP>1. Did we enable ack coalescing on the NCCL layer?

ashwin: ack coalescing is on by default, but the runtime does an early cudaEventQuery for backpressure detection. With more fragments the event queries happen more often and trigger host-side stalls.

perf-bot: repro commands:
  ./bench_tp --model test-gpt --tp 8 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --profile /tmp/prof.json
  flamegraph: /tmp/prof.json -> shows cudaEventQuery on main loop dominating wall time

ashwin: paste of small excerpt from perf.json:
```
NCCL: send(6.1KB) enqueue -> cudaEventQuery wait 78us
NCCL: send(5.2KB) enqueue -> cudaEventQuery wait 82us
GPU compute: kernel_fp16_small  avg 210us
GPU idle due to wait  310us
```

maria: can we tune batching heuristics to re-coalesce fragments at the runtime layer (pre-NCCL) so we keep compute kernel choice but reduce comm ops?

dylan: yes — two options: 1) revert chunk boundaries (coarser chunks) so msgs per all-reduce drop, 2) add a comm-coalesce stage that buffers small kv updates per step and emits a single larger NCCL op. Option 2 needs careful memory pressure control.

sam: also evaluate switching topology to tree for these small-msg regimes; tree reduces ring hops but cost model differs for fragmentation. We need param sweep.

ashwin: ran quick sweep:
  - coarser chunking (48KB) -> compute +8% but comm down -22% giving net +6% perf (win)
  - comm-coalesce buffer (5-10ms hold) -> reduces ops by ~70% but adds worst-case latency tail for first token
  - tree topology -> reduces per-step stalls by ~12% but increases peak bandwidth pressure on some links

maria: what about KV cache invalidation/refresh interaction? small-frag approach caused KV refresh to interleave with all-reduces, increasing contention?

ashwin: exactly. When we split updates, some TP replicas apply KV writes earlier which triggered async invalidation notifications. That created extra small control packets on top of data fragments.

perf-bot: note: regression first appeared after commit a3b9f2d (kernel-selector). Related PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3219

sam: tentative plan: revert the selector change for TP jobs by gate flag (runtime.env TP_COMM_SAFE=true) and implement runtime-level coalescer behind a tunable flag. Run 48h perf harness across tp in [2,8] and seqs [512,2048].

dylan: I'll prototype a coalescer that merges fragments upto 64KB or X ms flush whichever hits first. Keep telemetry on nvlink utilization and cudaEventQuery counts.

ashwin: for immediate mitigation — flip kernel selector to prefer previous chunking heuristics for tp>1. Added a quick patch: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/commit/ff12c9e (will roll to staging).

maria: please also add a small e2e regression test: micro-batch=1 TP run and assert step time within 5% of baseline.

ashwin: noted. I'll follow up with repro artifacts and flamegraphs in /internal/perf/2108123456.

sam: thanks. follow-ups: PR for coalescer (dylan), revert gate (ashwin), perf run (maria). I'll track in the runtime perf board. :thumbsup:
